items.q: And we found some people like Adelaide Hall, Margaret Simms.

ctx.x: to him about home and things like that. He was from Baltimore, and he would start drinking.

So I'll tell you about him after, but let me tell you about this show. Lyons brought this man in and this man heard us and he said, "I think that's what we need. But we've got to have a show." And Lyons said, "Don't worry about that, because I've got a choreographer here. Charles Davis can do that. And all he had to find was the necessary people. And we found some people like Adelaide Hall, Margaret Simms. And Eddie Rector didn't want to go, and neither did Johnny Higgins, see. So, we found others to take their…

But before that, then Lyons would start playing the Winter Garden. Every Sunday night, we started putting a show into the Winter Garden. I played the Winter Garden I guess, during around a year, I guess about 10 times. Sunday night concerts. And we was doing vaudeville at different times. And we started vaudeville when we was there, at Loew's vaudeville.
